Subject: MSA / Order Form – inspection boundary, pen-test window, & evidence ownership

Olga — thanks for the draft order form. A few quick things the security team asked me to clarify before we proceed to legal: 

1) Pen-test access: do you allow external testers to be given any form of privileged/system-level credentials, or is testing limited to customer-provisioned staging accounts? We need specifics to scope our internal risk approvals.

2) SOC 2 evidence cadence: Clarion typically asks for quarterly snapshots of SOC2-related artifacts and a 10-business-day turnaround on ad-hoc evidence requests. Can Redwood meet a 10-business-day SLA for evidence uploads?

3) Inspection boundary: our compliance folks want a short definition of what "inspection" covers (logs, configs, environment access, data samples). They also prefer a sampling approach vs. full-instance inspection.

I attached a quick spreadsheet with our initial questions (Clarion_Assurance_Qs.xlsx). If you can reply with where you land on the three items above we can loop in procurement/legal and move to redlines.

Thanks — Jared

Clarion Health

Team — forwarding Clarion's questions. High level proposal and asks below; please review and push back with legal language we should propose in the redline. I attached a proposed evidence rhythm PDF with timing and owners.

Summary proposal (ops + legal):
- Pen-test: allow external tests only against customer-provisioned staging tenants. No privileged or root credentials for third-party testers unless under supervised, on-site, or HSM-mediated access with an approved NDA.
- SOC2 evidence cadence: commit to quarterly artifact uploads to a shared secure drive + 10 business day SLA for standard evidence requests. For ad-hoc, we propose a 15-business-day window for anything that requires engineering-time (e.g., custom logs, full-scope exports).
- Inspection boundary: define inspection as "read-only access to pre-approved artifacts, logs, and sample datasets". Recommend sampling bands: up to 5% of sessions or a max of 50 records for sample exports unless specifically negotiated.

Next steps / owners:
- Karthik: draft redline language for the MSA/Order Form that limits inspection rights, defines notice periods (30 days for pen-test window), and enumerates evidence SLAs.
- Laura: confirm operational feasibility for 10-business-day uploads and identify which artifacts require engineering involvement.
- Olga: consolidate Clarion Qs, draft cover email and attach redline.

Proposed meeting: Thu 2026-12-03 10:00 PT (30m) to finalize legal asks before sending to Clarion.

Attachments: proposed_evidence_rhythm.pdf

Thanks — Olga

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-12-02T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA / Order Form – inspection boundary, pen-test window, & evidence ownership

Thanks — sounds reasonable. A few legal redline bullets I want included in the draft MSA/Order Form: 

1) Scoped Inspection: limit "inspection" to the specific, listed artifacts (SOC 2 reports, system-generated audit logs, configuration manifests, and agreed sample exports). Prefer to avoid an open-ended "inspect at will" clause.

2) Notice & Window: require 30 days written notice for any penetration test and a mutually agreeable 3-5 business day witness/observation window if Clarion insists on real-time testing. For remote testers, testing must be restricted to customer-provisioned test tenants and must never include privileged account credentialing by Redwood.

3) Evidence SLA & fees: accept the 10-business-day standard SLA for the listed artifacts, but for any ad-hoc requests that require engineering time we need an explicit "evidence fulfillment" effort bucket — propose a T&M or pre-purchase of evidence hours (e.g., 8 hours included per year, additional at retail).

4) Sampling: agree to a sample-based approach. Language should state a default sample cap (we suggest 5% or 50 records) with the ability to expand by mutual written agreement.

5) Data minimization & redaction: add a clause obligating the requester to accept redacted datasets where necessary to protect other customers and PII.

I'll draft specific redline snippets for the MSA and an Order Form appendix (redline_MSA_olga_v1.docx). Please confirm the proposed evidence SLA and whether operations can meet the 10-business-day target for routine items.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com

Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form – inspection boundary, pen-test window, & evidence ownership

Jared / Maya — thanks for the clarity. We reviewed with legal and ops and attached a consolidated redline and a proposed evidence rhythm. Key points we can commit to now: 

- Pen-test access: Redwood will only permit third-party testing against customer-provisioned staging tenants. We will not provide privileged/root credentials to external testers. For blue-team style observation we can provide a timeboxed witness window (3 business days) with prior notice.

- Notice & window: 30 days' written notice for planned penetration tests. For urgent security assessments (critical vulnerabilities), we'll treat those on a case-by-case basis but expect Clarion to provide at least 5 business days' notice when practical.

- SOC 2 / evidence cadence: Redwood will publish quarterly SOC2 artifact snapshots to a secure shared folder and will adhere to a 10-business-day SLA for standard evidence requests (controls mapping, policy docs, non-engineered logs). For items requiring engineering assistance (custom queries, bulk exports), we propose a 15-business-day SLA and suggest an evidence-hours bucket model (8 included hours / year by default).

- Sampling & redaction: default sampling cap of 5% up to 50 records per request; Clarion accepts redacted exports when required to protect unrelated customers/PII.

Attachments: redline_MSA_olga_v1.docx (specific contract language), proposed_evidence_rhythm.pdf (timing and owners).

Next steps:
1) Please confirm if the pen-test staging-only approach is acceptable.
2) If Clarion agrees, we'll send the MSA redline and ask procurement/legal to confirm the order form appendix and evidence-hours billing approach.
3) If you want a short sync, Karthik and Laura are available next week — suggested slots included in the shared calendar link.
